en: Verses of Homage to the Maṇḍala of Speech:
The goddesses beginning with Cakrī have one face, four arms, three eyes,
and very broad feet.
Seated upon the lotus of the navel, their channels purified, they are adorned with crowns set with excellent jewels. ||1||
I bow to the Black One who arises from the syllable *Ha*,
seated upon a red lotus on a corpse,
holding a flaying knife and a trident in her hands, and a spear and a skull-topped staff.
And Indra rests upon her lap.
In the petals, beginning with Carcikā and the others, there are [deities] consisting of staffs and tubes in sequence;
they face forward, turn clockwise, reside upon the petals, and have graceful limbs.
Terrible and fierce, with fangs like Time, her mouth ablaze with fire, possessing the speed of the wind, violent,
with fierce eyes and a thick nose, she dwells upon the petals of the lotus of the earth.
Carcikā and the others are in their respective directions.
Eight are indeed the forms of the illustrious Nāyikās, born from the syllables hi, bha, va, ya, yi, yṛ, hī, and jāta-kartī;
salutations here to those illustrious Yoginīs, and [others] born from iha, iha, u, yḷ, ṛ, yaṃ, and jāta-kartī. ||4||
In the lotus of the sun of Vārāhī, she has the reddish hue of a buffalo;
she is produced from the staff of the syllable *Haḥ*, marked by the white Śaṅkara,
and holds in her hands a staff, an excellent sword, and an excellent chain.
I bow down to her pair of feet, which are like a pestle upon Yama. ||5||
Kaṅkālī, Kālarātrī (three times), she of the enraged countenance, Kāladaṃṣṭrā (the tongue),
Karālī, Kālī, Ghorā, Virūpā, and Śūkarī upon the petals of the lotus and the earth.
The Yantra Goddesses: Eight [goddesses] possessing the splendor of the venerable Nāyikās arise from the staffs produced by *ṛ*, *ṝ*, *ṛ*, and *ṝ* born of the heart;
salutations here to those venerable Yoginīs, and also to those born from the staffs produced by *ru*, *ruḷ*, *ṛ*, and *raṃ*.
I bow to Raudrī, who resides upon a white bull and a red lotus in the Śuklottara [mandala], and who is born from the trident produced by the syllable *haṃ*;
she whose arms successively hold a trident and a *ḍamaru* drum.
Varuṇa holds a skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga) and a white serpent, while Yama holds them upon his lap.
Gaurī, Gaṅgā, Nityā, Svaparamantrīritā,
Trotalā, Lakṣmaṇā, Piṅgā, and Kṛṣṇā— these eight are the heroines on the petals of the lotus of the Vasu.
Wherein is Raudrī;
those born from the womb-born, water-born, fire-born, wind-born, and earth-born [beings] are equal to the illustrious Raudrī by means of the trident.
Salutation here to those glorious Yoginīs for the arising of the pain born from the syllables vu, vḷ, vaṃ, and ja. ||8||

Ainrī, who resembles her own color, whose lap is the earth of Danu, and who possesses a pure bow, arrows, and a bell, stands upon Varuṇa; she is born from Airāvata, Aruṇa, Padmagarbha, Jāyava, and Vajra.
And I bow to her whose lotus-like hand holds a bow. ||9||
Vajrābhā, Vajragātrā, Varakanakavatī, Urvaśī, Citralekhā,
Rambhā, Ahalyā, Sutārā, and Kamalavasudalā.
To the deity Vajrahasta;
to the eight Śrīnāyikās born from the heart, born from *la*, *li*, *ḷ*, and *hṛ*, and born from the vajra—homage here to those Śrīyoginīs: *ḷ lḹ laṃ*.
To those born from the emergence of the vajra. ||10||
Brāhmī, however, is seated upon a white lotus carried by a swan; she has the sun for her eye, and her yellow complexion is indicated by the four faces born from the earth.
In the northwest, she holds a water-born [lotus], a staff, and a water-pot.
I bow to the bowl upon whose lap sits Hari of cloud-like hue.
Sāvitrī is indeed lotus-eyed, possessed of water-born beauty, the mastery of intellect and speech,
Gāyatrī, the goddess Lightning herself, and also Smṛti within the lotus.
Obeisance here always to those Yoginīs who have the Vedas as their mouths and the deities presiding over them, who resemble the consort of Brahmā, and whose names begin with *kṣṛ*, *lā*, and *lī*.
By these—ḷ, kṣṝ, lu, ḹ, and la—arranged in their successive order, [the syllables] arise from the voids that have been produced. ||2||
I bow to Giriśa, who possesses the splendor of moonlight born from the lotus that arose at the beginning of time; he stands upon a lion, holds a white lotus,
and has a lotus-seed rosary, a thread, and jewels in his hands.
Seated upon her lap, Rasamukha indeed touched her foot. ||13||
Śrī, Cetā, Candralekhā, Śaśadharavadanā, Haṃsavarṇā,
Dhṛti, Padmeśā, Tāranetrā, and Vimalaśaśadharā are in the lotus of Īśa.
Salutations here always to those Yoginīs, who resemble Lakṣmī and bear their respective signs, [beginning with] KṢU-RĀ-RĪ.
By these [vowels]—ṛ, ṝ, kṣṝ, rū, r̥, lī, ī, ī, and raḥ—arranged in their successive order, [the syllables] are produced from the lotus-born [Brahmā]. ||14||
I bow to that maiden of the Kumāra-mantra, who resides in the southwest direction, who is marked by the emblem of the spear, who resembles the sun,
who stands upon a white lotus on a peacock, and who bears the insignia of Gaṇeśa. I bow to her— of whom...
And in her hands are a spear, a lotus, a noose, and an excellent goad. ||5||
The heroine is Padmānaṅgā, Kumārī, Mṛgapatinayanā, Ratnamālā, Sunetrā,
Klīnā, Bhadrā, Payoje, Varaśikhigamanā, and Nāyikā.
O King, here [is the mantra] for those Yoginīs who are equal to goddesses: *nama iha satataṃ yoginībhyaḥ kṣurārī*.
From these—*ṛ*, *ṝ*, *kṣṛ*, *rū*, *r̥̄*, and *raḥ*—arranged in their sequential order, [the Jewel-born] arises from the states of existence. ||16||
In the southeast (vahnau), Śrī-Vaiṣṇavī is seated upon a dark lotus produced by a discus; she is Garuḍa and marked with the four-faced one (Brahmā).
Her body is exceedingly black, and she holds a discus, mace, and lotus—
And salutations to her whose hand is marked with the supreme conch. ||17||
Śrī, Māyā, Kīrti, Lakṣmī, Svā, Parā, Vijayā, Śrījayā, Śrījayantī, and Śrīcakrī— these eight indeed reside upon the beautiful petals of the lotus in the directions of Vaiṣṇavī.
In this place,
let there be constant homage here to those yoginīs who resemble goddesses, [beginning with] KṢI-YĀ-YĪ.
By means of these—*yṛ*, *kṣī*, *yḷ*, and *yaḥ*—placed according to the rule of sequence, [the mantras] arising from the Jātacaraṇa-cakra [are formed]. ||18||
Indeed, on the left door and the left altar, from the seed-syllables produced by the consonants *ka, kha, ga, gha, ṅa* joined with two bindus,
there arose five [goddesses], beginning with Icchā, who are two-armed and moon-faced.
And from the letters of the *ca*, *ṭa*, *pa*, and *ta* groups produced from the eastern direction and so forth, even on the left side of the altar,
those five letters each are placed in every direction.
By means of the seed-syllables, elements, and their own respective signs. ||19||
Likewise, on the left altar, they are placed with those born from the *sa* class;
on the other moon arising to the left, they are likewise placed with those born from the *pa* class, and with that which is produced from the syllable *kṣa*.
Thus end the verses of homage to the maṇḍala of speech.
